title: FROM NEGROES TO GODS FROM EARTH TO GOLD

sense.text:
The Lord is asking Israel a question: “How happeneth it Israel, that thou art in thine enemies’ land”? How did we get into the position we are in, desolate at the bottom, on drugs, baby daddies, baby mamas, barely getting by? We are in the United States of America, the land of our enemies, dealing with lynchings now, our brothers hanging from trees, and these things are going to continue to happen. The Lord is asking, how is this happening to you, Israel?

“That thou art waxen old in a strange country”: you are not in your own land; you have waxed old in a strange country.

“That thou art defiled with the dead”: your mindset is defiled, abominable. The majority of our people are the walking dead, and before you woke up to the laws of God you were one of them.

“That thou art counted with them that go down into the grave”: Israel out of the way of God's laws is counted among the dead. This is the first scripture of the class, and the last one comes back to it: how did the gold become dim? How did we end up where we are?

precepts.why:
How did it happen that we are “defiled with the dead”? “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.” If you wander out of the way of the laws of God, you remain in the congregation of the dead.

Now you are the walking dead, a zombie out here. The majority of our people look like us, act like us, and we all grew up the same way. But you woke up to the laws of God. You were once that walking dead, that zombie that hated your people, that defiled sisters and brothers, stole from each other and did all manner of evil to each other. That is what it means to be defiled with the dead.

Now that we are in a strange country, what else has happened to us? “And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee”. That happened to all of us collectively. God gave us a heritage, and we lost it. “And I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not”: we serve our enemies, the other nations. “For ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever.” God said this would happen.

So we lost our identity, and once you lose your identity you have to have some kind of identity: African-American, Negroes, black, Jamaicans, Haitians, Puerto Ricans, Cubans and so forth.

“Thus saith the Lord; Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm”. We have been trusting in man a very long time: in this man's school system, his religious system, his political system. And where has it gotten us collectively? At the bottom of society. Sports, politics, Hollywood: no matter which way you turn, the Negro is always on the bottom. To make flesh your arm is to follow whatever man you think is going to lead you somewhere better than where you are.

“Hope deferred maketh the heart sick”. At the bottom of society, desolate, you come outside your door and there is a brother who looks just like you on the corner selling crack, another drunk at nine in the morning, a sister who looks just like you scantily clad, maybe selling herself. What do I have to look forward to here? If you come outside and see no opportunity for growth, your hope is deferred, and you say to hell with it, I am going to do what I need to do to survive.

Hope deferred makes the heart sick: it changes what is naturally supposed to be in you. Naturally you are supposed to grow spiritually and mentally, because innately you want to do the right thing. But the way we grow up in the hoods, we traumatize each other, family, friends, associates, teachers, pastors; one way or the other everyone is a victim of somebody's nonsense.

“But when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life.” When you get that flyer in your hand and see there is some kind of hope, it is a tree of life. Your mindset can be reprogrammed back to that God-level status, on your way to waking up and getting out of the situation you are in.

“Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land”. God has a problem with the black and Hispanic man and woman. “Because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.”

That is because our leaders will not teach it to us. Our leaders have failed us. They do not teach the laws of God; they teach go get money, beg Congress for some grants, vote Republican, maybe vote Democrat, maybe follow Jasmine Crockett, maybe follow Roland Martin, what about Al Sharpton? They put these people in front of us, but they are not leading us anywhere, and with all these leaders we collectively remain at the bottom.

No truth: and the leaders will not correct us or even call it out. No mercy: look on Instagram and TikTok and see how we do each other. No knowledge of God: you do not know God's word, what is required of you, or even that you are an Israelite.

“By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood.” We are a bunch of liars, we kill each other, we steal, we sleep with each other's women and men. Because these things are not corrected, “Therefore shall the land mourn, and every one that dwelleth therein shall languish”. Now we are desolate, the hope has been deferred, and we are going round in that toilet bowl trying to survive.

When Israel came out of Egypt and went into the land, we were supposed to destroy the nations, the Hittites, the Hivites, the Jebusites and the rest. “They did not destroy the nations, concerning whom the Lord commanded them: But were mingled among the heathen, and learned their works.” We mingled among the people we were supposed to remove from the land and learned how to serve their gods. What the hell is wrong with the Negro? “And they served their idols: which were a snare unto them”: we learned their groves and their stocks and worshipped them, and they were a trap to our people.

“Yea, they sacrificed their sons and their daughters unto devils”, just like today we have abortion. When Kamala Harris ran for president, she had Megan the Stallion, Cardi B, Usher and Magic Johnson, but the only issue she brought to the black community was abortion: no economic scholars to show how to improve the black community, no health people, nothing but how to legally kill your baby so you can keep being a sexual deviant. And here is the point: your leaders said nothing.

“And shed innocent blood”, “and the land was polluted with blood. Thus were they defiled with their own works, and went a whoring with their own inventions.” Because these things kept going unchecked, “Therefore was the wrath of the Lord kindled against his people, insomuch that he abhorred his own inheritance. And he gave them into the hand of the heathen; and they that hated them ruled over them.” Just like today: they that hate you pass laws and policies to keep you in the same position, and your leaders say nothing, or talk about Trump with no effect on your position. You remain at the bottom.

sense.text:
“Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me.” We innately already have these spirits inside of us. We are born with certain lusts, certain spirits.

And what has America done with those spirits? America cultivates them. To cultivate is to prepare and use for the raising of crops, to foster the growth of, to improve by labor, care or study, to refine. America refines these spirits within you, puts them on the forefront and makes them desirable, and entices our people to go after them. They put the worst examples of our people out front to make us desire that. You turn on Instagram and see the big-butt woman, and that spirit inside of you is enticed and enhanced and comes to the forefront. You may be battling homosexuality, and now you cannot watch a movie without seeing some man's bare ass. They put the LGBT stuff in there for your children to see. So they enhance and cultivate these spirits within us.

precepts.why:
These are the spirits we are born with: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness”. Evil thoughts proceed out of your mind. We battle fornication; there is the murder spirit, the thieving spirit, the covetous spirit; an evil eye toward your brother; blasphemy, lies against God; pride, too proud to be corrected.

“All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” They are already in us, and this is what America cultivates.

“This is the condition of the battle, which man that is born upon the earth shall fight”. Brothers and sisters, whether you know it or not, whether you are fighting or not, you are in a battle with these spirits. Are you just lying down and accepting your condition, or are you going to war? The majority of our people are best buds with Satan. You have to go to war with those spirits first and foremost within yourself.

The battle is one that man born upon the earth “shall fight”. Soldiers fight and go to war; weak men and boys just lie down.

sense.text:
“And that, knowing the time”: remember the young man in the video who got the flyer, changed his life, put on the purple and now is out waking up his people. Know the time. You see the times, and it is only going to get worse; you see the lynchings of our brothers and sisters, and they blame it on a black man. Stop playing games with us.

“That now it is high time to awake out of sleep”: you have been sleeping in Babylon, and you leaders have been asleep in Babylon way too long. “For now is our salvation nearer than when we believed.”

We have gone through it: how happeneth it, Israel; we lost our identity; we are destroyed for lack of knowledge; we came into the lands of our enemies, mingled among them and learned their works; they enhanced these evil spirits within us. Now it is high time to awake.

precepts.why:
Watch the prophecy; this prophecy is all of us right here. “For I knew that they would not hear me, because it is a stiffnecked people: but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves.” In the land of our captivities, right here in America, you are going to remember yourself. And you had better thank the Lord that he called you here. No captain or bishop called you; the Lord called you here.

“And shall know that I am the Lord their God: for I will give them an heart, and ears to hear”. The Lord puts that spirit on you to take another look at this Bible, not through the eyes of white supremacy like when you go to church, but through spiritual eyes. You realize we are all the people of this book, and we have to keep the commandments of God and believe in his son Jesus the Christ.

“And they shall praise me in the land of their captivity, and think upon my name, And return from their stiff neck, and from their wicked deeds”: return from being hardheaded, no more a Negro. “For they shall remember the way of their fathers, which sinned before the Lord.” We remember that our fathers did all kinds of foolishness, and we go the other way, no matter who does not like it: your family, your fathers, so what. “And I will bring them again”.

That is the prophecy: you wake up, hear this Bible, repent and begin to do the works of the Lord. That is waking out of sleep.

sense.text:
This is Moses setting up the leaders after Israel came out of Egypt. The people were bringing their burdens to Moses, and his father-in-law told him to set it up this way. The whole class is aimed at the leaders of Israel, current and future: how we deal with the people, how we motivate them, how we take care of those in our charge.

“Take you wise men”: wise men, not dummies. “And understanding”: men that have understanding. “And known among your tribes”: there are a lot of wise men with wisdom and knowledge, but should we follow everybody who has certain wisdom? What is missing is that they are known. Al Sharpton is known; people follow him not because he keeps the commandments, but because he has influence. To be known is to have influence: a certain level of knowledge, and people know you, so you can move the people one way or the other.

So a leader has to be known. A leader is not supposed to be meek-mouthed in the back, quiet. You are supposed to be lions. A lion roars; there is no such thing as a quiet lion. We are not raising anybody to be a damn introvert. We are raising lions who go out on the streets and bring forth God's words with power.

“So I took the chief of your tribes”: the best of your tribes, “wise men, and known”, men with influence who could move the body, and made them heads over you, “captains over thousands, and captains over hundreds, and captains over fifties, and captains over tens, and officers among your tribes.” These are rulers, and the next verse shows they are judges.

“And I charged your judges at that time”. In verse 15 he calls them captains and officers; in verse 16 he tells you what you are going to be doing: judging matters. If you have ten men under you, you judge the matters between those ten brethren; a thousand is a greater burden. “Hear the causes between your brethren, and judge righteously between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him.” To judge matters you have to know the law.

precepts.why:
A leader has to be known, so he cannot stay quiet. “I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, which shall never hold their peace day nor night”. As an Israelite man, as a leader, you are never supposed to hold your peace.

“Ye that make mention of the Lord, keep not silence”: ye that bring out the scriptures, do not keep silence. Your job is to go out and spread forth the glorious gospel of your Lord and Savior Jesus the Christ with power. We are not looking for meek-mouthed soft dudes.

If we are supposed to be replications of Christ, we have to understand the spirit Christ had in him. “The Lord shall go forth as a mighty man”: we are supposed to be just like that, mighty men. “He shall stir up jealousy like a man of war: he shall cry, yea, roar”. He roars to the people; a lion does not whisper. “He shall prevail against his enemies.”

That is the spirit we must have when we go out to teach the people. That is what leaders do: influence the people.

Being known, having a reputation, comes from experience. These were “two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown”: leaders of the assembly, famous in the congregation.

Renown is widespread fame, within the body and outside it; respect and acclaim earned through great achievements or character. How do you garner respect? By showing a pattern of good works. That is someone who has influence, and people will follow someone with influence. That is what “known among your tribes” means.

A good leader needs certain qualities, or he will destroy lives and destroy spirits: physical features, knowledge, integrity, vision, initiative, motivation skills, self-confidence, social skills, communication skills and decisiveness. We are all works in progress on them, but we are all working to get them.

Physical features: if you are overweight, in the red, trying to lead people who are in the green, they will listen but look at you like this guy is full of it; he cannot even lead himself away from the table. When Bishop Nathanyel, with Bishop Kai and other brothers, met the prime minister of the Bahamas, Bishop had his hair pulled back; it came loose while he was talking, and the prime minister turned and said, let me talk to this guy over here. Bishop changed it and cut it, because we are ambassadors of Christ, and we have to play that part. Knowledge: you have to know what you are talking about in this word, or the people will see it.

Integrity is being honest and having strong moral principles that you refuse to change even when no one is watching. “Wherefore, my beloved, as ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence”. Not just when people are looking at you: when nobody is watching you have to maintain your moral principles.

A leader must have a vision. If there is no clear vision, the people will not follow you wholeheartedly; they will be around, but they will only go so far with you. Maybe the short-term vision is turning the grass outside into a parking lot, or getting another building. But if you are just there doing nothing and breaking bread every week, they will not follow. “Where there is no vision, the people perish”: they eventually go back into the world and are destroyed.

The rest of the qualities: initiative is acting and making decisions without being told; a good leader sees a problem and solves it, not turns a blind eye. Brothers in camps have admitted they saw sisters doing wrong and turned a blind eye, and sisters do not respect men who let them act however they want; they only tolerate them. Motivation skills get the best production out of brothers and sisters. Self-confidence: if the people do not see you confident in what you believe, they will not follow you or bring you what is going on in the body. Social and communication skills: this is the most socially awkward generation, talking through emojis and GIFs, and you have to communicate effectively. Decisiveness: make a decision. If everybody likes your decision, you are trying to please the people, and that will destroy them. Take advice, but at the end of the day the leader makes the decision.

The real job of a leader is not being in charge; it is taking care of those in your charge. As an officer over ten, those ten men bring you their issues and you help them fix them. If a brother on the video editing team is battling porn, he puts the work aside to scroll, hours go by and he misses the deadline. Help him get over it and he can concentrate on the work of the Lord; do that for ten men and the production multiplies ten times.

Part of being a leader is knowing when to give responsibilities to men. “It is not reason that we should leave the word of God, and serve tables. Wherefore, brethren, look ye out among you seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business.” This is the same thing Moses had to do, and there were criteria for leadership.

Then look at the production: “And the word of God increased; and the number of the disciples multiplied in Jerusalem greatly; and a great company of the priests were obedient to the faith.” When they put responsibilities on brothers of good report, the word of the Lord increased. That is what good leaders are able to do.

This is Paul after he was knocked off the horse and blinded, now teaching Christ. “And he spake boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus, and disputed against the Grecians”. He spoke like a lion, boldly, not soft. “But they went about to slay him”: when you speak boldly in the name of the Lord, eventually they are going to want to put hands on us.

This is the result of good leadership: “Then had the churches rest throughout all Judea and Galilee and Samaria, and were edified; and walking in the fear of the Lord, and in the comfort of the Holy Ghost, were multiplied.” Everybody walking in the fear of the Lord with the Holy Ghost on them, and they multiplied. When we are all rolling in the same spirit, those on the outside come in and say, I want to be a part of this; I want the spirit these brothers and sisters have.

sense.text:
As a leader you have to sacrifice: your time, your family, your friends, maybe your job, your well-being. Leadership comes at great personal sacrifice. “That ye present your bodies a living sacrifice”: when you come to Christ you are going to sacrifice something one way or the other; there is no way around it.

“Holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.” It is your reasonable service to be a living sacrifice, because however many years you lived before you repented, you spent doing dumb stuff, being a wicked Negro. Now you find out we are the children of God and there is a way out, so you sacrifice your time, your energy, your body, friends, family, associates, money and your lust.
“The elders which are among you I exhort”: the elders in this context are the leaders among you.

“Feed the flock of God which is among you”. What are you supposed to feed them, burgers and French fries? You feed them the word of God.

“Taking the oversight thereof”: if I take the oversight, I am an overseer. I am checking out the body, what is going on here and there, and making a report of it.

“Not by constraint, but willingly”: you are not supposed to be forced to be a leader. Leadership is not for everybody; everybody does not have the same spirit. You do it willingly, as a sacrifice.

“Not for filthy lucre”: not for money. No leader is supposed to manipulate you to get money out of you personally, crying month after month so members keep giving him money. That is evil. “But of a ready mind”.

“Neither as being lords over God’s heritage”. Nobody is supposed to be lording over you. The world says we are a cult that tells you what to do and where to move. No: we counsel you out of the scriptures and you decide how you move. If you move according to the scriptures, all praises to the Most High; if you move against them and cannot get it right, you have to go. Nobody is lording over you, but to stay here you have to conform to the word of God. Your job as a leader is not to lord over or intimidate, not to be a dictator or a tyrant. The people are not supposed to fear you; they are supposed to respect you.

“But being ensamples to the flock.” Every one of the qualities of a good leader, integrity, initiative, self-confidence, even the physical, goes into being an example, so those under you can see it and want that spirit. If they see things in you that are not right, they veer away and the respect is not there.
“And when the chief Shepherd shall appear”: the chief Shepherd is Christ. “Ye shall receive a crown of glory that fadeth not away”: we will be in the kingdom, immortal.

“Likewise, ye younger, submit yourselves unto the elder.” He was speaking to the elders, the leaders; now he speaks to the younger: submit to the leader. “Yea, all of you be subject one to another”: you stay in your order and I stay in mine. “And be clothed with humility”: humility is freedom from pride or arrogance, being humble. If you think you are better than your brothers and sisters, how are you better when we are all collectively still at the bottom? We went into slavery together and were born in the ghettos of America together. What are you arrogant for?

“For God resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble.”
“Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.”

“Be sober, be vigilant”: be sober, brothers; be vigilant, leaders. “Because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”. Satan devours us through our own lust and temptation, and he destroys a body through division, gossip, disunity, doubt, confusion, miscommunications and grudges.

precepts.why:
What happens when you lord over the flock? “The fear of the Lord goeth before the obtaining of authority”: before you get a position, you have to have a healthy fear of God. “But roughness and pride is the losing thereof.” Lording over the flock, hurting the flock and quenching its spirit, is how you lose it.

“Unto the servant that is wise shall they that are free do service”: unto the leader that is wise, the people will willingly follow and serve. “And he that hath knowledge will not grudge when he is reformed.” When he is corrected, he will not hold a grudge or take it personal. When leadership visits a school, the leader of the school gets in his feelings: that was wrong, I don't agree. Take the correction and move the hell on. Just shut up and take it. Yes sir, I will fix it. A leader that cannot take correction has a dangerous spirit.

“For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”. Correction is the way of life, and everyone is going to be corrected. Everybody. So what are you mad for? I didn't like the way it was corrected; I thought I was doing a good job. So what? Do not get sensitive and emotional. Just fix it, take the correction and move the hell on. That is submitting yourselves to the elder.

Be clothed with humility, not that arrogance that you are better than your brothers and sisters. “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” That is the pride being spoken of: too proud to be corrected.

A lot of sisters have that spirit: a sister will not even correct another sister for fear it will turn into an argument. That is an evil spirit. If someone comes to you with a scripture and says, according to this you are not supposed to be moving that way, and you go bucking, you are not bucking against him; you are bucking against the word of God. It is not his word; he just brought it to you. A heart turned away from his Maker is a dangerous position to be in.

“Wherefore he saith, Awake thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead”: awake, you brothers, you leaders that are asleep; arise from your dead estate. “And Christ shall give thee light”: Christ gives you the understanding.

“See then that ye walk circumspectly”. Circumspect is thinking very carefully about possible risks and consequences before acting or saying something. As a leader you cannot speak out of place or speak from your emotions; you think about the risks and the consequences before you move and before it comes out of your mouth. “Not as fools, but as wise”. That is how a leader stays vigilant against the devices of the adversary.

Why is it dangerous for a leader to believe nobody can do this but me, none of this would be possible without me? That is a self-willed spirit, a prideful spirit, the spirit of a novice. That leader is making himself out like he is God, and he can hurt the congregation.

“That ye might learn in us not to think of men above that which is written”: learn in us, the leaders, not to think of us above that which is written. “That no one of you be puffed up for one against another.” When you are puffed up you think you are better than your brother, high and mighty, and everybody else beneath you. It is an insult to say none of this is possible without me, because it says y'all are nobody without me. God resists the proud.

“And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.” It is the same point: the Lord can use anyone. The Lord will bring down one and raise up another, so no leader can say nobody can do this but me.

Why does a leader need trustworthy people around him? He needs men who will tell him if he is wrong and tell him if he is right according to the scriptures, with no partiality; men to be his eyes and ears and tell him what is going on in the flock, as Moses set up other leaders.

“These are murmurers, complainers, walking after their own lusts”. The murmurer and complainer does not murmur to the leadership; he murmurs to the members of the body. Then when he gets in front of a leader, he uses flattery to persuade him. “And their mouth speaketh great swelling words, having men’s persons in admiration because of advantage.” I may be your friend, you may have an affinity toward me, and I can use that against you: I have you on a string, I can manipulate you and smile, and even get you to promote me when I do not deserve it.

That is why you have to have a tight circle, men you trust who are trustworthy and will tell you the truth about yourself. Division and flattery are among the adversary's devices.

sense.text:
Say you fixed the issue, you have been examining yourself and you see the errors in your ways. “Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault”: you lost your rank for whatever reason. “Ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness”: so that man can be restored.

So do not be in your feelings, sitting in the back. There are leaders who were once over schools, got taken down for their own evil, and then made excuses not to come to class anymore: I missed the meeting because of this, I missed Sabbath class because of that. Trust and believe the body is watching. The men you once led see you are full of it and see that you were never genuine.

precepts.why: “The fear of the Lord goeth before the obtaining of authority: but roughness and pride is the losing thereof.” Some leaders get brought up and some get brought down; that is part of the journey of being a leader. Roughness and pride is the losing of that position, because you are harming the people one way or the other. That is the fault that takes a man's rank, and Galatians shows how he is restored.

“For promotion cometh neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the south. But God is the judge: he putteth down one, and setteth up another.” When you cannot get the job done or you are harming the body, God sets somebody else in your place. Promotion and demotion are in God's hand.

sense.text:
See how David acted under king Saul. “And David went out whithersoever Saul sent him, and behaved himself wisely: and Saul set him over the men of war”. He was not king yet, and Saul promoted him. How did David behave himself? Wisely. You men are supposed to behave yourselves wisely, not as children, not jesting all the time like everything is a joke. Even you young men: it is war outside, and people that look like us are hanging from trees on a regular basis.

“And he was accepted in the sight of all the people, and also in the sight of Saul’s servants.” That is a promotion, and David behaved himself wisely in it.

“The women came out of all cities of Israel, singing and dancing, to meet king Saul”, and said, “Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands.” There is nothing wrong with the man under you having a skill set better than yours. Your job is to lead, not to be the best at everything. If the men under you did a great job, it means you did a great job. Your glory is the next brother's glory; we all have on the same shirt and the same agenda, getting the kingdom of heaven.

But Saul saw something different. “And Saul was very wroth, and the saying displeased him”. He was not at one with David and the men under him; he was in his feelings, in his emotions. “And what can he have more but the kingdom?” Remember, Saul is the one who promoted David.

“Therefore Saul removed him from him, and made him his captain over a thousand”. He was captain over all the king's army, and now captain over a thousand: a demotion. “And he went out and came in before the people.”

“And David behaved himself wisely in all his ways; and the Lord was with him.” Did David get in his feelings because he was put down? No. Some of you brothers are very emotional, you hold grudges, you want to be the best at everything, and that is not the quality of a good leader. If I do not have your skill set I send you to do the job, and when you get the accolades I get them too, because we all have on the same damn shirt.

Because David behaved himself wisely, the Lord was with him. The Lord is not with you when you are in your emotions with all these thoughts that have to be said. Shut up.

precepts.why:
“Now therefore keep thy sorrow to thyself”. Shut up with all that moaning and crying; save that for the sisters. You are a man, a leader. Stop the emotion. They did that to me and I don't feel it's right: be quiet. When they see you see the error of your ways, you can be restored, but in the meantime you are a soldier, an officer of ten, whatever the case may be.

“And bear with a good courage that which hath befallen thee”: take your demotion and keep it moving. Some brothers act like they are all right, but at Sabbath class they are way in the back instead of up front where they belong, or they stop coming and start missing meetings. You are out of order and you are not in the fight.

“And therefore shake off thy great heaviness, and put away the multitude of sorrows, that the Mighty may be merciful unto thee again, and the Highest shall give thee rest and ease from thy labour.” Shake off the little punk heaviness and put away your little sorrows.

How did David deal with a promotion and with a demotion? In all ways he behaved himself wisely. “Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully”. That is easy to say and hard as hell to do, but we must conform our minds to it and practice it. Even if you feel you were wrongfully demoted, take it cheerfully. Christ took his tribulation, and this is not even tribulation; it is a rank in a school. We all need to be humbled one way or another, clothed with humility.

“And be patient when thou art changed to a low estate.” Be patient: that does not mean sit in the corner after class and soak, or be passive-aggressive, stepping away from your duties and doing them half-ass because you were made a soldier. That willful neglect is not the spirit of the Lord. As a man of God, rank or not, you should be doing the work.

“Woe unto you that have lost patience! and what will ye do when the Lord shall visit you?” Destruction to you when you lose patience in your emotions.

“As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers”. If the leadership in your camp is weak, the men and women under it will be weak. You can always judge the leadership by how the brothers and sisters in the congregation move: if they move reckless, the brothers leading are weak; if they move in order, these brothers are bringing forth fruits meet for repentance. That is why a leader has to behave himself wisely.

sense.text: “Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord”. You are not getting any kingdom if you are bearing grudges and bitterness.

“Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you”. If you do not follow peace with all men and you have issues with brothers and sisters, a root of bitterness springs up in you, and if you do not fix it you are going to be out the door. “And thereby many be defiled”.

Sister A has a problem with sister B and works it out with visiting leadership. At class she is seated next to sister B, gets up after ten minutes and goes to sit next to the newest sisters. That petty garbage goes on where leaders are weak and emotional. Confronted, she says, she apologized, but I'm just not ready to get over it yet. It is time for you to go. What scripture says it is going to take you time to get over it?

“Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.” Paul is speaking of being unforgiving, and he compares you to Esau. You have an Edomite spirit when you cannot forgive your brother or sister. “For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.” If you are unforgiving, there is no kingdom for you; you are just like Esau.

When grudges go unchecked, you leaders had better move and speak up at the table. Do not let certain spirits fester in the body to infect other spirits; your job is to protect the spirits in the body. If one sheep is sick, you do not leave it with the rest to infect them; you remove it.

precepts.why:
“Take heed to yourselves: If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him”: if somebody offends you, correct them, which sister A did not do at the time. “And if he repent, forgive him.” Not hold a grudge, not be bitter, not tell them it is going to take time: forgive him.

If you cannot forgive, stay your ass home. Stay your black or Hispanic behind home. We do not want that spirit in the body until you fix it.

“Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone”. Alone: sisters, do not tell your husband so that spirit jumps on him against her husband; brothers, do not tell your wife so she gets in her feelings and defends you when you may be wrong.

“If he shall hear thee”: if he repents, oh bro, I didn't know that offended you, my bad. “Thou hast gained thy brother.” The point of Matthew 18 is not to have somebody put out of the body; it is to gain your brother or sister back.

“But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.” The witnesses hear the case at the same time. “And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the church”: the leaders, you judges. “But if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican.” Get him up out of here. You will not repent; you are like a heathen, an Edomite.

sense.text: “But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The house of Israel is a great house. The gold and the silver represent the honorable; the wood and the earth represent the dishonorable.

“If a man therefore purge himself from these”: these are the dishonorable brothers and the dishonorable sisters. As the gold and the silver you have to remove yourself from the wood and the earth, the ones always in trouble, whose names are always coming up in some foolishness, in and out of the body, who cannot get it right. Purge yourself from them and nothing is in your way: “he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified”, cleansed, “and meet for the master’s use”, a productive member of the body, “and prepared unto every good work.”

“Flee also youthful lusts”. What do young men and men in general battle with? Lust: your porn addiction, your lust for the big-butt woman, for other women, maybe even for men. As a leader you must flee youthful lust. “But follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart.” Those that call on the Lord with a pure heart are the gold and the silver; that is where you are trying to go, not with the wood and the earth.

“But foolish and unlearned questions avoid, knowing that they do gender strifes.” Avoid those stupid questions. Here comes the apologist at camp with a phone in your face: is Jesus God, what about the Trinity? You already know what spirit he is rolling in, and he will edit the footage to shame the ministry.
“And the servant of the Lord must not strive; but be gentle unto all men, apt to teach, patient”. A leader must know how to teach the word of God.

“In meekness instructing those that oppose themselves”: those that oppose themselves are the vessels unto dishonor, the wood and the earth. The topic has not changed. When you see brothers going the wrong way, you must have the skill to draw that brother out of the fire, “if God peradventure will give them repentance to the acknowledging of the truth; And that they may recover themselves out of the snare of the devil, who are taken captive by him at his will.”

precepts.why: “But shun profane and vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness.” Paul is repeating himself. Say we are on Clubhouse talking about the immaculate conception; the brother gives the scriptures but it is going nowhere, turning into an argument, back and forth. It genders strife: nobody gets edified, it turns into a shouting match, then disrespect, and the people listening at the bottom say this doesn't sound right; I don't hear the scripture coming out, just stuff I don't want to hear.

When an idiot comes in your face with a camera asking stupid questions that have been answered a thousand times, do not let him embarrass you. “Answer not a fool according to his folly”: he is looking to embarrass you in his folly. “Lest thou also be like unto him.” When you entertain that spirit, he can put the footage up and shame the body.

This is one long letter; the topic is not changing. “This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, Without natural affection”, without natural affection toward their brothers and sisters, “trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent”: all over the place, following no guideline, no law, no discipline; “fierce”, angry; “despisers of those that are good, Traitors, heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God”.

“Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof”: these are the vessels of dishonor, the wood and the earth. They have a form of godliness but deny the laws of God and follow no law. “From such turn away.” Not entertain them: turn away from those brothers that are dishonorable and leave them the hell alone. That is purging yourself from these.

“For of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts”. That goes back to fleeing youthful lusts: the silly women who come into the body not knowing a thing, and he props himself next to her and says he is her counselor now. That is the wood and the earth.

sense.text: How do you grow? When you come into a leadership role, and when you come into the body at all, these are the things you have to do: “Wherefore laying aside all malice”: we cannot be malicious toward each other; “and all guile, and hypocrisies”: we cannot be hypocrites; “and envies”: we cannot envy and be jealous of each other; “and all evil speakings”: we cannot speak evil of and slander each other.

“As newborn babes”: when we decide to deal with those spirits and come into the body, we are babes in Christ. “Desire the sincere milk of the word”: want, yearn for the sincere milk of the word, the laws of God. “That ye may grow thereby”. You have to get rid of these spirits, malice, guile, hypocrisies, envies and evil speakings, and repent and keep the word and apply it, in order to grow.
“If so be ye have tasted that the Lord is gracious.”

“How is the gold become dim!” Brothers, we are supposed to be gold and silver, and now we are wood and earth. This goes back to the first scripture: how happeneth it, O Israel? How the hell did we get into the position we are in, hating each other, killing each other, like clockwork, round and round on the mouse wheel every year: killing each other, selling drugs, getting a new baby mama, robbing each other.

“How is the most fine gold changed!” You brothers are the most fine gold. It is not up to anyone else whether you believe it; you have to believe it for yourself. These are not his words or your words; this is what God said about you. “The stones of the sanctuary are poured out in the top of every street.”

“The precious sons of Zion, comparable to fine gold”: God said it, and you have to choose to believe it. “How are they esteemed as earthen pitchers, the work of the hands of the potter!” You went from gold to earth. That is the whole class: from Negroes to gods, from earth to gold.

precepts.why:
“I will make a man more precious than fine gold”. That is what God said: one more time for the black man, I will make a man more precious than fine gold, “even a man than the golden wedge of Ophir.”

The precious sons of Zion became earthen pitchers, but God will make them gold again. That is the turn from earth to gold.
